hints.title: Preserve All Users
hints.text: Users who have taken no rides must still appear in the output with a distance of 0.

hints.title: Outer Join and Sum
hints.text: Perform a left join from Users to Rides on user_id.

hints.title: Null Coalescing
hints.text: Aggregate distance with sum, wrapping it in coalesce to replace null with 0, and order by user_id ascending.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
SELECT 
    u.user_id,
    u.name,
    COALESCE(SUM(r.distance), 0) AS `traveled distance`
FROM Users u
LEFT JOIN Rides r ON u.user_id = r.user_id
GROUP BY u.user_id, u.name
ORDER BY u.user_id ASC;
```

complexity.notes: Left join followed by grouping on user_id and sort.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Inner join omits users with zero rides, violating the specification.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(U) hash table state for aggregation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use LEFT JOIN and COALESCE to handle users without rides.

solutions.code:
SELECT 
    u.user_id,
    u.name,
    COALESCE(SUM(r.distance), 0) AS `traveled distance`
FROM Users u
LEFT JOIN Rides r ON u.user_id = r.user_id
GROUP BY u.user_id, u.name
ORDER BY u.user_id ASC;

SELECT 
    u.user_id,
    u.name,
    COALESCE(SUM(r.distance), 0) AS "traveled distance"
FROM Users u
LEFT JOIN Rides r ON u.user_id = r.user_id
GROUP BY u.user_id, u.name
ORDER BY u.user_id ASC;

import pandas as pd

def get_total_distance(users: pd.DataFrame, rides: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    merged = users.merge(rides, on="user_id", how="left")
    merged["distance"] = merged["distance"].fillna(0)
    res = merged.groupby(["user_id", "name"])[["distance"]].sum().reset_index()
    res = res.rename(columns={"distance": "traveled distance"})
    return res.sort_values("user_id")
